name: Aman, who ensnared Achiacharus
charge: Treachery against the man who brought him up
summary: Tobit's dying counsel to his son holds up one case: remember how Aman handled Achiacharus that brought him up, how out of light he brought him into darkness, and how he rewarded him again. Achiacharus, the king's cupbearer and Tobit's kinsman, had once interceded for Tobit himself.
offense: Ingratitude become betrayal, against a benefactor who stood as a father. The story assumed by the text is the tale of Ahikar: the adopted nephew who forged evidence to have his uncle executed.
judgment: Achiacharus was saved, but the other had his reward: for he went down into darkness. Aman fell into the snare and perished. Tobit's moral: consider what alms doeth, and how righteousness doth deliver.

entries.commentary: As snow in summer and rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool. As the bird wandering and the swallow flying, the causeless curse shall not come. A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back. Ecclesiasticus says the same: correction and work are for a servant, and that correction is the rod for the fool's back. -

Do not answer a fool according to his folly, lest you become like him. Many of us have argued with an idiot and been made to look like an idiot; onlookers wonder why you are even arguing with him. Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit. He that sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks damage.

The legs of the lame are not equal, and so is a parable in the mouth of fools. As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he that gives honor to a fool. As a thorn goes up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools. Like a splinter driven under the skin, it hurts and can take days to work out.

The great God that formed all things both rewards the fool and rewards transgressors. As a dog returns to his vomit, so a fool returns to his folly. Second Peter calls this a true proverb, showing the apostles quoted Solomon: those who escape the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Christ and then are again entangled are worse off than at the beginning. -

Do you see a man wise in his own conceit? There is more hope for a fool than for him. The slothful man says there is a lion in the way and in the streets. As the door turns on its hinges, so the slothful turns on his bed; he hides his hand in his bosom and it grieves him to bring it back to his mouth. The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.

He that passes by and meddles with strife not belonging to him is like one that takes a dog by the ears. Ecclesiasticus warns not to strive in a matter that does not concern you. A young lady who tried to break up a high-school fight was grabbed by police, slammed face-first, and left with brain damage; the Bible is a true book. As a madman who casts firebrands, arrows, and death, so is the man that deceives his neighbor and says, "Am I not in sport?" -

Where there is no wood the fire goes out, and where there is no tale-bearer the strife ceases. As coals to burning coals and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindle strife. The words of a tale-bearer are as wounds that go down into the innermost parts of the belly. Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.

He that hates dissembles with his lips and lays up deceit within, so when he speaks fair, do not believe him, for there are seven abominations in his heart. Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shown before the whole congregation, put out on display. Luke says nothing is covered that shall not be revealed. Watch for spirits that flatter you with kind words while carrying deceit; that thing will be revealed, so pray to the Most High. -

Whoever digs a pit shall fall in it, and he that rolls a stone will have it return upon him. A lying tongue hates those that are afflicted by it, and a flattering mouth works ruin. That flattery is deceit.

This is the prayer that we all have, especially us as Israel. We want the Most High to fight against those who fight against us. That is a righteous prayer that our forefather David had. This is the prayer we have for everybody that comes against us. If you do not feel like that, then you do not believe in the Bible. David is praying that the same destruction his enemies want to bring on him falls on them instead. That is what we have to understand: the Most High is not a god of saving everybody, he is a god of destroying our enemies. He has been that way and it is not going to change.

The salvation David rejoices in is the destruction of his enemies. That is what salvation is. You cannot be saved if you still have to answer to your enemies. You do not save the wolf and the sheep together. They just came out with more footage about Ahmaud Arbery saying the brother was still alive when the police came, and the one who shot him admitted it, and the police still let them go home. These are the things we have to pray for. That is the salvation we are looking for. We do not worship a God that saves our enemies alongside us. No matter what we think, Esau is too strong for us right now. He owns a military. Black people do not own a military. You may be able to fight one and win, but we do not own a military. We are behind enemy lines. They took over this country and we still have not taken it back. The Most High is the only one who is going to save us from that one who is stronger than us. That is what David prophesied about the nation of Israel.

False witnesses rise up and lay to our charge things we knew not. That happens with us right now. You have our own brothers claiming we are with the Rosicrucians, sold out to the Illuminati, that we wear purple because we had to choose a color. The most racist people in the world are not going to recruit us. We have our own money; we gave out gold coins worth a million dollars at the 2015 or 2016 Passover. They rewarded evil for good, but when they were sick, David's clothing was sackcloth and he humbled his soul with fasting. That is praying for your enemies and for those that despitefully use and persecute you. You do not go railing for railing. You defend yourself, but you do not turn around and do something wicked back to them. When they were down, David felt their pain just as they had felt it. That is how we have to move. David bowed down heavily as one that mourns for his mother, but in his adversity they rejoiced and gathered themselves together against him. When our school got hit by a tornado, people on Facebook and all social media were rejoicing, saying all praises to the Lord that a tornado hit our school. But those same people, when they needed help, we were there. A lot of it we did not say anything about, because this is the prayer we had: let the Most High look on it and see how we move and how they move, and let him judge that. Our feast days are full of hypocrites, people who do not have the betterment of their people at heart. They come to the feast days, the new moons, the sabbaths, and sit there wicked, crept in unawares. It always happens. This is what David was talking about when he spoke of hypocritical mockers in feast.

David cries out asking how long the Most High will look on, and asks him to rescue his soul from their destructions. He asks that his enemies not wrongfully rejoice over him nor wink with the eye that hate him without a cause. When we fall or do something, they point and mock, "Aha, aha, I have seen it." No matter what happens, you have to keep the commandments of the Most High and keep your faith in him. When everybody is against you, keep your faith. That is the example David set.

David asks the Most High not to keep silence, to stir up himself and awake to his judgment, and to judge him according to his righteousness. He prays that his enemies not say in their hearts, "We would have had it," or "We have swallowed him up," but that they be brought to confusion. There are people not in the body who see what we go through and pray the best for us. Brothers from a lot of different backgrounds saw what we went through as a body and said they pray the best for us. That is a righteous thing to have. But the ones who do not, the prayer is to let them be brought to confusion, along with all the stuff they talk all the time.

verses.text: And bury me decently, and thy mother with me; but tarry no longer at Nineve. Remember, my son, how Aman handled Achiacharus that brought him up, how out of light he brought him into darkness, and how he rewarded him again: yet Achiacharus was saved, but the other had his reward: for he went down into darkness. Manasses gave alms, and escaped the snares of death which they had set for him: but Aman fell into the snare, and perished.

Wherefore now, my son, consider what alms doeth, and how righteousness doth deliver. When he had said these things, he gave up the ghost in the bed, being an hundred and eight and fifty years old; and he buried him honourably.

And there passed not five and fifty days, before two of his sons killed him, and they fled into the mountains of Ararath; and Sarchedonus his son reigned in his stead; who appointed over his father’s accounts, and over all his affairs, Achiacharus my brother Anael’s son.

And Achiacharus intreating for me, I returned to Nineve. Now Achiacharus was cupbearer, and keeper of the signet, and steward, and overseer of the accounts: and Sarchedonus appointed him next unto him: and he was my brother’s son.

And I knew not that there were sparrows in the wall, and mine eyes being open, the sparrows muted warm dung into mine eyes, and a whiteness came in mine eyes: and I went to the physicians, but they helped me not: moreover Achiacharus did nourish me, until I went into Elymais.
And Achiacharus, and Nasbas his brother’s son, came:
Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.
For without cause have they hid for me their net in a pit, which without cause they have digged for my soul.
Let destruction come upon him at unawares; and let his net that he hath hid catch himself: into that very destruction let him fall.

lawsResolved.text: You shall not deal falsely or treacherously with your brethren.
Punishment will come to those who attempt to gain by deceit.
Punishment is the fruit and reward for iniquity and wicked ways (you shall reap that which you sow).
